title: Federal Tort Claims Act postal-matter exception
shortTitle: Federal Tort Claims Act postal-matter exception
summary: Section2680(b) preserves immunity for claims arising from loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission of letters or postal matter.
notes:
The provision is an exception to the Act’s broader waiver for specified employee torts. Raila and Dolan interpret the terms together, limiting the exception to delivery failures such as lost, delayed, damaged, or misdirected mail and the resulting harm, rather than all injuries occurring during postal delivery.

That construction allows the pleaded slip-and-fall claims to clear the particular immunity barrier. It leaves the remaining prerequisites and merits of liability to further proceedings. The treatment reports the statutory version and cases discussed by Katzmann; it is not a later-law update.
